29 October 2026. Independent analytic construction; root has whole-read and accepted the mathematical chain at its stated scopes, subject to the finite-slice insertion clarification now made in Section 6. The bounded-cut packet is frozen and has separately passed root review. No new normal-fluid fixture is run here: the physical qualifier below changed the destination before such a computation.

Use the actual stable conjugate-flavor model `H=b†Tb+c†conjugate(T)c+sum_i U_i(nb_i-nc_i)^2`, with T>=0, U_i>=0. At L symmetric imaginary-time slices, whiten the HS fields x in R^(ML), and put

`theta_(i,l)=sqrt(2 beta U_i/L) x_(i,l)`,

`B(x)=F_L ... F_1`, `F_l=exp[-(beta/L)T] diag(exp(i theta_l))`.

Cyclic collection of symmetric half steps preserves the canonical trace; every factor is a contraction. For fixed phi and `z=r exp(i phi)`, r<1, define

`f(x)=log |det(I-zB(x))|^(-2)`.

The conditional grand field potential is `V_alpha(x)=|x|^2/2-alpha f(x)`, with alpha in [0,1]. This section supplies the actual global curvature condition; log-concave sampling is an established ordinary method, not a new generic algorithm.

A first derivative inserts one diagonal generator, so

`||B'[v]||F<=sum_l a_l<=sqrt(2 beta Umax)||v||2`.

`||B''[v,v]||1<=(sum_l a_l)^2<=2 beta Umax ||v||2^2`.

These bounds have NO volume, topology, hopping-norm or slice-count factor. They do not require commuting hopping and phase factors.

`f''[v,v]=2 Re Tr[R z B''+R z B' R z B']`.

`chi=4 beta Umax r/(1-r)^2`.                         (1)

# A global normal-fluid operation, with its physical ceiling

29 October 2026. The proof has passed root's whole analytic review. This is a mathematical sampler/normalizer construction; no new Langevin execution or physical data acquisition is claimed.

For the native stable conjugate-flavor model

`H=b†Tb+c†conjugate(T)c+sum_i U_i(nb_i-nc_i)^2`, `T>=0`, `U_i>=0`,

the actual finite-slice auxiliary-field potential has a topology-, bandwidth- and slice-independent Hessian perturbation bound

`||Hess log|det(I-r exp(i phi)B)|^(-2)|| <=4 beta Umax r/(1-r)^2 =chi`.

When chi<1, this supplies the missing global mixing interface on ANY hopping graph: native matrix products acquire the entire gradient in O(L M^3) arithmetic, and an explicit Euler/Girsanov receiver gives a polynomial TV guarantee. Positive bounded-ratio annealing acquires the field normalizer without a pressure oracle. Strong-convexity sampling and annealing are established ordinary methods; the contribution is their qualified native admission, not a new generic MCMC algorithm.

The same representation exposes why this does not yet supply the sought ordered-matter capability. At fixed fugacity r<1 the EXACT physical full opposite-flavor pair density matrix has norm at most `[r/(1-r)]^2`. The finite-slice insertion is generally complex and is not called a positive density matrix: the proof passes fixed-sector insertions and uniformly summable number tails to exact Gibbs first. At fixed beta Umax, a divergent pair eigenvalue would force the present curvature gate to close. Large beta times hopping bandwidth alone does not repair that gate.

For a canonical count of grand mass b, the inherited ceiling is only `[r/(1-r)]^2/b`; b remains a paid input. No arbitrary prescribed-density or ordered-phase conclusion follows.

# Whole review of the topology-independent normal-fluid sampler

29 October 2026. Root read global_curvature/PROOF.md and reconstructed its
native product derivatives, acquired gradient, discrete sampling and physical
ceiling. The construction is accepted at that analytic scope. No new bulk
calculation or independent sampler execution is claimed.

Slice Cauchy--Schwarz and contraction sandwiches correctly pay B' in
Frobenius norm and B'' in trace norm without a volume/slice/hopping factor.
The determinant Hessian bound is chi=4 beta Umax r/(1-r)^2. Prefix/suffix
products acquire its gradient with a uniformly conditioned resolvent. For
chi<1 the full interpolating field actions are strongly convex. Gaussian
start entropy, Euler second moments and the explicit interpolation path-KL
bound pay discrete Langevin TV error. Bounded adjacent annealing ratios
then pay normalizer acquisition; no gradient or target-law oracle is supplied.

At a collected finite-L cut, offdiagonal insertions are averages of complex
non-Hermitian matrices, not automatically a positive finite-L physical state.
Root identified this distinction and the producer made it explicit. Their
norm bounds still hold; fixed-sector convergence with uniform r<1 polynomial
number-insertion tails passes them to exact Gibbs. The resulting one-body
and FULL opposite-flavor pair-space operator bounds are c and c^2, with
c=r/(1-r). Exact canonical conditioning spends its count probability.

Thus large kinetic bandwidth or a flat-band degeneracy does not acquire an
interaction-ordered phase in the fixed-r admitted grand ensemble. Divergent
pair eigenvalues force the curvature gate to shrink beta U with volume.
This exact qualifier redirected work before an unnecessary normal-fluid
fixture. It is not a general critical-matter hardness theorem. Strong
canonical AFQMC, cluster/Borel, tensor and number-conserving alternatives
retain their actual access; no practical or historical advantage is claimed.
